breakthroughs.title: Movable type (China)
breakthroughs.why: Bi Sheng's reusable ceramic characters showed that a page could be assembled from interchangeable pieces instead of carved as one block.

breakthroughs.title: Mechanical clock escapement
breakthroughs.why: The verge-and-foliot escapement made purely mechanical clocks possible. In the 1370s alone, more than 70 European cities added public clocks.

breakthroughs.title: Printing press (Europe)
breakthroughs.why: Gutenberg's metal-type press made books something that could be produced in volume. By 1500, Western Europe's presses had printed over 20 million copies.

breakthroughs.title: Steam engine
breakthroughs.why: Newcomen's engine near Dudley Castle was the first practical steam engine. It drained mines and gave industry power that did not depend on wind, water or animals.

breakthroughs.title: Photography
breakthroughs.why: The daguerreotype, announced in Paris in 1839, was the first practical photographic process. For the first time, a moment could be captured and reproduced without an artist's hand.

breakthroughs.title: Electric telegraph
breakthroughs.why: Samuel Morse's first public message, "What hath God wrought," travelled from Washington to Baltimore in 1844. News could now move faster than any messenger.

breakthroughs.title: Telephone
breakthroughs.why: Bell's patent, issued in March 1876, covered sending speech over wire. The telephone did not become commercially viable until about 1878.

breakthroughs.title: Central electric power station
breakthroughs.why: Edison's Pearl Street Station began supplying electricity to customers in Manhattan in September 1882, the forerunner of the central power station.

breakthroughs.title: Wright Flyer
breakthroughs.why: The first sustained, controlled, powered flight, in December 1903, started the age of aviation.

breakthroughs.title: Commercial radio broadcasting
breakthroughs.why: KDKA's first scheduled broadcast aired the 1920 election returns. Within four years the US had 600 commercial radio stations.

breakthroughs.title: Penicillin
breakthroughs.why: Fleming noticed a mold that stopped staphylococcus bacteria from growing. It took roughly another decade for its full medical significance to be recognized.

breakthroughs.title: Transistor
breakthroughs.why: Bell Labs demonstrated the first transistor on December 23, 1947, a solid-state alternative to the unreliable vacuum tubes of the time.

breakthroughs.title: ARPANET
breakthroughs.why: The first message crossed the ARPANET, forerunner of the modern internet, on October 29, 1969. The system crashed after two letters.

breakthroughs.title: World Wide Web
breakthroughs.why: Tim Berners-Lee opened the Web to the public in 1991. CERN's choice to make it completely open let it spread freely.

breakthroughs.title: iPhone
breakthroughs.why: Apple announced the iPhone in January 2007 and began US sales in June. A software kit for outside developers followed in March 2008.

breakthroughs.title: ChatGPT
breakthroughs.why: OpenAI released ChatGPT as a free research preview on November 30, 2022. By January 2023 it had reportedly passed 100 million users.
